original_value: To date, automatic driving technology has become a hotspot in academia. It is necessary to provide a personalization of automatic driving decision for each passenger. The purpose of this paper is to propose a self-learning method for personalized driving decisions. First, collect and analyze driving data from different drivers to set learning goals. Then, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm is utilized to design a driving decision system. Furthermore, personalized factors are introduced for some observed parameters to build a personalized driving decision model. Finally, compare the proposed method with classic Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithms. The results show that the performance of the personalized driving decision model is better than the classic algorithms, and it is similar to the manual driving situation. Therefore, the proposed model can effectively learn the human-like personalized driving decisions of different drivers for structured road. Based on this model, the smart car can accomplish personalized driving.

result.paraphrase: Automatic driving technology has recently become a major research focus in academia. To personalize autonomous driving decisions for each passenger, this paper proposes a self-learning approach for personalized driving decisions. First, driving data from different drivers are collected and analyzed to establish learning objectives. Next, the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm is used to build a driving decision system. In addition, personalized factors are added to certain observed parameters to construct a personalized driving decision model. Finally, the proposed method is compared with classic Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithms. The results indicate that the personalized driving decision model outperforms the classic algorithms and is comparable to manual driving. Therefore, the model can effectively learn human-like personalized driving decisions for structured roads, enabling smart cars to perform personalized driving.
